name: HK Express livery
description: White, with deep purple sweeping down from the fin across the rear fuselage to the belly behind the wing, a white tail cone; a white lowercase 'e' (with a white tick before it and a teal square after) big on the purple fin; huge purple 'HKexpress' along the forward fuselage. Purple engines; teal-and-purple sharklets.

sources.note: Low-cost subsidiary of Cathay Pacific since 2019; rebranded as HK Express in 2013-14 with the purple scheme.

sources.title: HK Express Airbus A321 B-LEG, Taiwan Taoyuan, 2026 (CC BY-SA 4.0, Bahnfrend)
sources.note: Left side, climbing: the purple sweep, fin logo, titles, engines, sharklets (measured on the photo rotated level).

sources.title: Hong Kong Express Airways B-LEK, 2024-11-02 (CC BY-SA 4.0, LN9267)
sources.note: From below and the left, climbing: the purple reaches under the rear fuselage; teal sharklet tips.

areas.name: purple sweep from the fin down across the rear fuselage to the belly; white tail cone behind

logos.description: HK Express's 'e': a white lowercase e drawn as a thick open spiral (the crossbar curling in from the right), a short white slanted tick like an apostrophe before it at upper left, and a small teal square turned 45 degrees at its lower right. The same artwork on both sides.
The 'e' small in white on the sharklet's purple inner face (seen on the far wing).

titles.style: Very large, over and through the forward windows from the first door almost to the wing: 'HK' in condensed capitals, 'express' in a rounded lowercase whose e's echo the spiral 'e' and whose r ends in a ball; medium-bold, upright.

notes: Drawn from a 2026 photo of an A321ceo (the A320s and A321neos wear the same). The purple's forward edge is a curve, steep at the crown and sweeping forward at the belly. Sharklets: the near one's outer face reads teal in the photos, the far one's inner face purple with the 'e'; low confidence on which face is which color. Belly not seen squarely aft of the wing beyond the purple's reach. Not drawn: the registration. Re-checked 2026-11-15 against B-LEG (A321, 2026) and B-LEK (2024-11-02): HK Express's commonest type is the A321 (its photos are all A321s), so drawnOn A321; on the measured A320 shape (0.9x the length) the title and purple sweep come out a little longer as shares than on an A320 itself. Title place, height and length agree with B-LEG; lowercase 0.68 of the capitals. The purple sweep's edges were left as drawn.
history: New in this dataset (Skyarium v1 had no HK Express entry). The purple scheme came with the 2013-14 rebrand from Hong Kong Express Airways to a low-cost carrier; unchanged under Cathay ownership since 2019.
